name: Prolog
typeSystem: Dynamically typed terms with no static type checking; unification operates on tagged terms such as atoms, numbers, variables, and compound terms.
runtime: Typically compiled to implementation-specific virtual-machine instructions; some systems also compile to native code

runtimes.name: Prolog VM (SWI / SICStus)
runtimes.role: Programs compile to implementation-specific virtual-machine code derived from or related to the Warren Abstract Machine.

runtimes.name: GNU Prolog (native)
runtimes.role: Can compile programs to standalone native executables.

compilers.name: SWI-Prolog
compilers.role: Popular implementation with a virtual-machine compiler and rich libraries.

concurrencyModel: Implementation-dependent; SWI-Prolog supports native threads with message queues

codeExample.source:
parent(tom, bob).
parent(tom, liz).
parent(bob, ann).

ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Y).
ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Z), ancestor(Z, Y).

?- ancestor(tom, ann).
